mainTopic: Two holinesses on one animal: רבי מאיר's תפוס לשון ראשון versus רבי יוסי, and קדושה דחויה for the animal and its תמורה
overview: Our משנה records a dispute about a person who says over one animal, "the תמורה of an עולה, the תמורה of a שלמים." רבי מאיר says only the first holiness takes hold. רבי יוסי says both take hold if he meant both from the start. רבי יוחנן narrows the dispute. Everyone agrees about "this, and afterward this" (only the first counts) and about "this only if that" (both count); the argument is only about the in-between wording of our משנה. The גמרא then brings ברייתות about an animal declared half one offering and half another. These show that רבי מאיר's rule is truly תפוס לשון ראשון, which is why the order of עולה and חטאת matters to him. Another ברייתא, following רבי יוסי, teaches that a half-עולה, half-שלמים animal is holy but not offered, and its תמורה is not offered either, because it comes from קדושה דחויה. Finally רבי יוחנן brings a partners' animal consecrated one half at a time, which is holy but never offered; his ruling continues on the next עמוד.

steps.title: Agreed case one: one holiness after the other
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says everyone agrees that if a person says "let this take effect, and afterward let this take effect," only the first statement counts.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: רבי יצחק son of רבי יוסי said in the name of רבי יוחנן: Everyone agrees about someone who says "Let this holiness take effect" and afterward "Let this holiness take effect." In that case all agree that we hold on to the first statement only.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens with רבי יוחנן marking off the first case where רבי מאיר and רבי יוסי do NOT argue. If someone clearly sets up one holiness after another, only the first one takes hold.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the first holiness, עולה, lands on the animal, the animal is already taken. The second holiness, שלמים, has nowhere to go. This gives us one edge of the dispute: a clear 'one after the other' statement.

keyTerms.meaning: Everyone agrees; the dispute does not apply here
Let it take effect / take hold (said about holiness)
Hold on to the first wording; only the first statement counts
According to everyone

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רבי יוסי argues here. Even רבי יוסי agrees that a clear "first this, then that" statement gives only the first holiness.

phrases.english: GEMARA:
Rabbi Yitzḥak, son of Rabbi Yosei, said
that Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
Everyone agrees about one who says
"Let this take effect" and afterward "Let this take effect" —
phrases.notes: The first "this" is the עולה holiness and the second is the שלמים holiness.

phrases.english: all agree: we hold on to the first statement.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא on the משנה's dispute between רבי מאיר and רבי יוסי.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When one says "let this take effect and afterward let this take effect," only the first holiness takes hold, according to everyone.

steps.title: Agreed case two: one holiness depends on the other
steps.stepSummary: Everyone also agrees that if a person says "this shall not take effect unless that one takes effect too," both holinesses take hold.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he said: "This holiness shall not take effect unless that holiness also takes effect," then both holinesses take hold on the animal.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן gives the second case where everyone agrees, the opposite edge. Here the person makes each holiness depend on the other, so both take hold.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first case the person lined the holinesses up one after the other, so the first one blocked the second. Here he tied them together as a condition, so neither can come in alone. The result is that both land together. Now we have two clear edges, and the dispute must sit somewhere in between.

keyTerms.meaning: Unless; sets up a condition
Both of them
Are consecrated / become holy

phrases.english: "This shall not take effect
unless this one takes effect" —
both holinesses take hold.

steps.triggerLanguage: לֹא תָּחוּל זוֹ אֶלָּא אִם כֵּן חָלְתָה זוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second agreed case, the opposite of step 1, which completes the frame around the dispute.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When one makes one holiness depend on the other, both take hold, according to everyone.

steps.title: Where they argue, and רבי מאיר's reasoning
steps.stepSummary: The dispute is only about the wording of our משנה, "תמורת עולה תמורת שלמים." רבי מאיר says repeating the word תמורה makes it like "one after the other," so only עולה takes hold.
steps.simpleTranslation: They argued only in a case like our משנה, where he said "the substitute of an עולה, the substitute of a שלמים." רבי מאיר holds as follows. He could have said "the substitute of an עולה and שלמים," but instead he said "the substitute of an עולה, the substitute of a שלמים." So he is like someone who says "let this take effect, and afterward let this take effect."
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן now places the dispute in the middle case: the wording of our משנה. He explains why רבי מאיר says only the first holiness takes hold.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר pays attention to the extra word. A person who wanted both holinesses together would have said it in one phrase: "תמורת עולה ושלמים." Saying "תמורה" twice sounds like two separate statements. That matches agreed case one (step 1), so only עולה takes hold.

keyTerms.meaning: They only argued about; narrows a dispute to one case
Our משנה
A substitute animal that becomes holy in place of a holy animal
Since he should have said; reasoning from the wording he did not use
Burnt offering / peace offering

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a key method: the גמרא reads a person's exact wording, including the words he could have used but did not, to decide what he meant.

phrases.english: They argued only in a case like our mishnah,
where he said, "the substitute of a burnt offering, the substitute of a peace offering,"
for Rabbi Meir holds:
since he could have said
"the substitute of a burnt offering and peace offering,"
and instead he said, "the substitute of a burnt offering, the substitute of a peace offering" —
he is like one who says
"Let this take effect and afterward let this take effect."
phrases.notes: This is agreed case one, so only the first holiness, עולה, takes hold.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After setting the two agreed edges, places the dispute in the middle and explains רבי מאיר.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי מאיר, repeating "תמורת" makes the statement count as one holiness after the other, so only the עולה holiness takes hold.

steps.title: רבי יוסי explains why the person repeated the word
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי answers רבי מאיר's argument. The person repeated "תמורת" on purpose. Saying "עולה ושלמים" in one phrase might sound like an animal that is holy but can never be offered.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוסי holds: If he had said "the substitute of an עולה and שלמים," I would have thought the animal is holy but cannot be offered. So his repeated wording teaches us something.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains רבי יוסי's side. It answers רבי מאיר's point that the person "should have said" it in one phrase.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר read the repeated "תמורת" as a sign of two separate statements. רבי יוסי gives it a different reason. A single phrase could sound like a split animal that is holy but cannot be brought. By repeating "תמורת," the person shows that he wants both holinesses on the whole animal from the start. That puts the case closer to agreed case two, where both take hold.

keyTerms.meaning: I would have thought; a possible mistaken reading
Holy but cannot be offered on the מזבח
It teaches us; this shows the purpose of the wording

steps.whatToRemember: רבי מאיר: the extra "תמורת" means two statements, one after the other, so only עולה takes hold. רבי יוסי: the extra "תמורת" was said on purpose to avoid a bad reading, so both holinesses take hold if he meant both from the start. Everyone agrees about the clear cases at the two edges.
steps.confusionAlert: רבי יוסי is not saying the animal actually gets offered as both. He is explaining why the speaker chose this wording. The point is only that the person meant both holinesses from the start.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yosei holds:
if he had said, "the substitute of a burnt offering and peace offering,"
I would have said it is holy but cannot be offered,
so it teaches us.
phrases.notes: Repeating "תמורת" shows he wants each holiness on the whole animal.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי מאיר's "he should have said" argument by giving another reason for the repeated wording.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains the extra word another way: it was said to prevent a misreading, not to separate the statements.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Saying "תמורת עולה ושלמים" might mean a split animal that is holy but cannot be offered.
steps.terutzMaskana: Repeating "תמורת" shows he intended both full holinesses from the start, so both take hold according to רבי יוסי.

steps.title: A ברייתא on an animal that is half substitute for an עולה and half for a שלמים
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא records a dispute. רבי מאיר says the whole animal is offered as an עולה. חכמים say it grazes until it becomes blemished and is sold, and the money is split between the two offerings.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבנן taught: If someone says, "This animal, half of it is the substitute of the עולה and half of it is the substitute of the שלמים," all of it is offered as an עולה. These are the words of רבי מאיר. חכמים say: it grazes until it gets a blemish, it is sold, and with half its money he brings a substitute עולה, and with half its money a substitute שלמים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא with a case like our משנה, except here the person splits one animal into halves. רבי מאיר and חכמים argue about it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר stays consistent with Step 3: when the person repeats his words ("half... and half..."), only the first statement counts, so the עולה takes hold on the whole animal. חכמים hold that both holinesses take hold. One animal cannot be offered as two different קרבנות, so it waits for a blemish and its money is used for both offerings.

keyTerms.meaning: Half of it (the animal)
It grazes until it becomes blemished, so it can be redeemed
And it is sold, once it is blemished
With the money (value) of

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think חכמים are saying the animal has no holiness. They hold it has two holinesses. That is exactly why it cannot be offered and has to be sold after it gets a blemish.

phrases.english: The Sages taught: One who says
"This animal, half of it is the substitute of the burnt offering
and half of it is the substitute of the peace offering"
all of it is offered as a burnt offering,
these are the words of Rabbi Meir.
And the Sages say: it grazes until it becomes blemished,

phrases.aramaic: וְתִימָּכֵר, וְיָבִיא בִּדְמֵי חֶצְיָהּ תְּמוּרַת עוֹלָה
phrases.english: and it is sold, and with the money of half he brings a substitute burnt offering
and with the money of half a substitute peace offering.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: הָאוֹמֵר בְּהֵמָה זוֹ חֶצְיָהּ תְּמוּרַת עוֹלָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא that applies the רבי מאיר / חכמים dispute to an animal split into halves
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי מאיר: the whole animal is an עולה. חכמים: both holinesses take hold, so the animal is sold after it gets a blemish and the money is divided between the two offerings.

steps.title: רבי יוסי: if he meant both from the start, his words stand
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי says that if the person intended both holinesses from the beginning, his words stand, because nobody can say two names at the same moment.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי said: If that was what he meant from the start, then since it is impossible to say two names at once, his words stand.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא ends with רבי יוסי's opinion. He says the person's full statement counts, not just the first half.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This answers רבי מאיר's "first statement wins" approach. A person has no way to say two words at once, so if he planned both halves from the start, the second half is not a later addition. Both holinesses take hold.

keyTerms.meaning: He intended this from the beginning

keyTerms.term: אִי אֶפְשָׁר לְהוֹצִיא שְׁנֵי שֵׁמוֹת כְּאַחַת
keyTerms.meaning: It is impossible to say two names (designations) at the same moment
His words stand (all of them take effect)

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי: אִם לְכָךְ נִתְכַּוֵּון מִתְּחִלָּה,
phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei said: If that was his intent from the outset,
since it is impossible
to say two names at once,
phrases.notes: "Names" means the holy labels, like עולה and שלמים.

phrases.english: his words stand.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a third opinion to the same ברייתא
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If both holinesses were intended from the start, both take effect, since two names cannot be said at once.

steps.title: Isn't רבי יוסי saying the same thing as חכמים?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that רבי יוסי's view looks the same as the view of חכמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי is the same as חכמים!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא. Why would רבי יוסי be quoted separately if he holds just like חכמים?
steps.deeperAnalysis: חכמים already said that both holinesses take hold. רבי יוסי also says both take hold. A ברייתא normally does not list two names for one opinion, so the extra line seems pointless.

keyTerms.meaning: That is the same as

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei is the same as the Rabbis!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions why the ברייתא lists רבי יוסי separately from חכמים
steps.kashyaTarget: The wording of the ברייתא, which lists רבי יוסי as a separate opinion
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Both opinions say both holinesses take effect, so the separate listing seems redundant.

steps.title: רבי יוסי is the one teaching the whole view of חכמים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the whole opinion of חכמים is really taught by רבי יוסי. His line explains the reason for it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי teaches the whole thing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question. רבי יוסי is not a separate opinion. He is the author of the view of חכמים, and his line gives its reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: "חכמים" in this ברייתא is really רבי יוסי. His closing statement, that two names cannot be said at once, is the explanation for why the animal must be sold. So the ברייתא is not repeating itself.

keyTerms.meaning: He teaches all of it (he is the author of the entire statement)

steps.whatToRemember: In the first ברייתא there are really two sides. רבי מאיר says only the first statement counts. רבי יוסי (called חכמים) says both holinesses take hold.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei teaches all of it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the objection of Step 7
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reattribution: the opinion of חכמים is identified as רבי יוסי's own
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יוסי and חכמים are two separate opinions that say the same thing
steps.terutzMaskana: There is one opinion, taught by רבי יוסי. His line explains the reasoning behind it.

steps.title: A second ברייתא: half עולה and half חטאת
steps.stepSummary: Another ברייתא brings the case of an animal declared half עולה and half חטאת. רבי מאיר says the whole animal is offered as an עולה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another ברייתא teaches: "An animal, half of it is an עולה and half of it is a חטאת." All of it is offered as an עולה. These are the words of רבי מאיר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second ברייתא. Now the two halves are an עולה and a חטאת, and רבי מאיר rules first.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר applies his usual rule: only the first statement, עולה, takes hold. The עולה holiness then spreads over the whole animal, so it is all offered as an עולה.

keyTerms.meaning: Sin offering

phrases.english: It is taught in another baraita:
"An animal, half of it a burnt offering and half of it a sin offering"

phrases.aramaic: כּוּלָּהּ תִּיקְרַב עוֹלָה, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי מֵאִיר.
phrases.english: all of it is offered as a burnt offering; these are the words of Rabbi Meir.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a second ברייתא with עולה and חטאת instead of two substitutes
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי מאיר: only the first designation, עולה, takes hold, and the whole animal is offered as an עולה.

steps.title: רבי יוסי: the animal must die
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי says the animal declared half עולה and half חטאת must be left to die.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי says: it must die.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי disagrees with רבי מאיר about the עולה / חטאת animal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Just as in the first ברייתא, רבי יוסי holds that both holinesses take hold. One animal cannot be offered as both an עולה and a חטאת. Because one half is a חטאת, it is not sold the way the first animal was. It is left to die.

keyTerms.meaning: It must die (left alone until it dies, not offered and not redeemed)

steps.confusionAlert: Compare this with Step 5. There, the animal with two holinesses was sold after it got a blemish. Here, because a חטאת is involved, it is left to die instead.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei says: it must die,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives רבי יוסי's opposing view in the second ברייתא
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Both holinesses take hold. Since the animal cannot be offered, it is left to die.

steps.title: Both agree: if חטאת is said first, the animal must die
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא ends with a point of agreement. If the person says "half חטאת and half עולה," both רבי מאיר and רבי יוסי agree the animal must die.
steps.simpleTranslation: And they agree that if someone says "half of it is a חטאת and half of it is an עולה," it must die.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא closes by showing where רבי מאיר and רבי יוסי agree. The case is the same split, but with the order reversed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי מאיר, word order is everything. When עולה was said first, he ruled the whole animal is an עולה. When חטאת is said first, he does not reach that result, and he agrees with רבי יוסי that the animal must die. The ברייתא states the agreement without spelling out the reason.

keyTerms.meaning: And they (both sides) agree

steps.whatToRemember: For רבי מאיר the order of the words decides the case. "Half עולה, half חטאת": the whole animal is an עולה. "Half חטאת, half עולה": it must die. רבי יוסי says it must die either way.

phrases.english: And they agree regarding one who says
"Half of it a sin offering and half of it a burnt offering" that it must die.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends the second ברייתא with a case where both sides agree
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: When חטאת is said first, both רבי מאיר and רבי יוסי agree the animal must be left to die.

steps.title: Who is agreeing to whom?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks who is giving in when the ברייתא says both sages agree. The answer is רבי מאיר.
steps.simpleTranslation: "They agree." Whose view is being stated here? רבי מאיר's.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא looks at the word "they agree" (שוין) from Step 11. It asks which sage is giving in to the other, and answers that it is רבי מאיר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי always says the animal must die, so his agreement is nothing new. The real news is that רבי מאיר, who usually says "offer it as an עולה," agrees here that the animal must die.

keyTerms.meaning: They are equal, meaning they agree
Who is it? Whose opinion is this?

phrases.english: "They agree": who is this?
phrases.notes: This points back to the end of the ברייתא, where both agree the animal dies when חטאת is said first. So who is the one giving in here?

phrases.english: Rabbi Meir.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the agreement stated at the end of the ברייתא in Step 11.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which sage is giving in to the other in the case of "half חטאת, half עולה"?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי מאיר gives in and agrees that the animal must die.

steps.title: Isn't that obvious?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that it is obvious רבי מאיר would agree here, so why did the ברייתא need to say it?
steps.simpleTranslation: That is obvious!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא. Why did it need to tell us that רבי מאיר agrees in this case?
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first case ("half עולה, half חטאת"), רבי מאיר follows the first words, so the animal is an עולה. By the same logic, if חטאת is said first, the first words make it a חטאת, and it must die. So his agreement seems to follow automatically.

keyTerms.meaning: It is obvious. Used to ask why something needed to be said at all.
Sin offering
Burnt offering, burned completely on the מזבח

phrases.english: That is obvious!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the need for the ruling that Step 12 says comes from רבי מאיר.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's statement that רבי מאיר agrees the animal dies when חטאת is said first.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If רבי מאיר follows the first words, then saying חטאת first obviously makes it a חטאת. There seems to be no need to teach this.

steps.title: Showing that רבי מאיר's reason is "go by the first words"
steps.stepSummary: The ruling was needed. Without it, we might think רבי מאיר's reason is that a mixed חטאת can be offered. Then even "half חטאת first" would be offered. The ברייתא shows that this is not so.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said: if the ברייתא had not told us, I would think רבי מאיר's reason is not "go by the first words." Instead, his reason would be that a חטאת mixed with something else can be offered. Then even if someone said "half חטאת" and afterwards "half עולה," the animal would be offered. The ברייתא teaches us that this is not so.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the "it's obvious" challenge. The ברייתא's last line was needed to rule out a different way of understanding רבי מאיר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There were two possible reasons for רבי מאיר's ruling in the first case. One is "go by the first words." The other is "a mixed חטאת can be offered." If the second were true, the order of the words would not matter, and the animal would be offered either way. The ברייתא says he agrees the animal dies when חטאת comes first. That proves his reason is the first one, תפוס לשון ראשון.

keyTerms.meaning: You might have said. Introduces a mistaken idea that the teaching comes to rule out.
I would have thought (the mistaken first idea)
Hold on to the first words. Only what a person says first takes effect.
A חטאת mixed with another kind of holiness in the same animal
It comes to teach us

steps.whatToRemember: רבי מאיר's rule is תפוס לשון ראשון. The first words decide what the animal is. That is why "half עולה, half חטאת" is offered as an עולה, but "half חטאת, half עולה" must die.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't think רבי מאיר holds that a mixed חטאת can be offered. The גמרא brings up that idea only to reject it.

phrases.english: You might have said:
if it had not taught us this,
I would have said that Rabbi Meir's reason
is not because of "hold on to the first words,"
rather, this is the reason:
a mixed sin offering is offered.
phrases.notes: In this mistaken idea, the חטאת part being mixed in would not stop the animal from going on the מזבח.

phrases.english: And then even when he said "half of it is a sin offering,"
and afterwards said "half of it is a burnt offering," it would be offered.
So it teaches us that it is not.
phrases.notes: Since רבי מאיר agrees the animal dies here, his reason must be "go by the first words."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the "it's obvious" challenge of Step 13.
steps.terutzResolutionType: The ruling is needed to rule out a mistaken reason (a מהו דתימא answer).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי מאיר's reason is that a mixed חטאת can be offered, so the order of the words would not matter.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי מאיר's reason is תפוס לשון ראשון, so when חטאת is said first the animal must die.

steps.title: An animal declared half עולה and half שלמים
steps.stepSummary: Another ברייתא: an animal declared half עולה and half שלמים is holy but is not offered. It can make a תמורה, and the תמורה has the same status.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another ברייתא teaches: if someone said, "This animal, half of it is an עולה and half of it is שלמים," it is holy but is not offered. It can make a substitute (תמורה), and the substitute is just like it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא. Now the two halves are an עולה and a שלמים instead of an עולה and a חטאת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even though both offerings are ones a person may bring as gifts, the animal still cannot go on the מזבח with two different holy statuses. Still, the holiness is real: it can make a תמורה, and that תמורה gets the same rules as the animal itself.

keyTerms.meaning: Peace offering, partly eaten by the owners
It is holy, but it is not brought on the מזבח
A substitute: a regular animal swapped for a holy one, which then becomes holy too
Like the one it came from (same status)

phrases.english: It is taught in another ברייתא:
If one said: "This animal, half of it is a burnt offering
and half of it is a peace offering,"
it is holy, but it is not offered;
it makes a substitute,
and its substitute is like it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a new ברייתא with a similar split declaration, now עולה and שלמים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An animal declared half עולה and half שלמים is holy but not offered. It makes a תמורה, and the תמורה has the same status.

steps.title: Whose opinion is this ברייתא?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which sage the ברייתא follows, and answers: רבי יוסי.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose view is this? It is רבי יוסי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks which sage the ברייתא from Step 15 follows. It answers that the ברייתא follows רבי יוסי. This sets up the next question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier in the סוגיא, רבי יוסי held that a person is held to both parts of what he says. So when someone says 'half עולה, half שלמים,' both statements count. That fits the ברייתא's ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: Who is it? (Whose opinion does this teaching follow?)

phrases.english: Whose view is it? It is רבי יוסי,
phrases.notes: This is about the ברייתא from the last step: an animal declared half עולה and half שלמים.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Identifies the author of the ברייתא quoted in Step 15.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא is the source of the ruling about half עולה and half שלמים?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי יוסי, who holds a person to both parts of his statement.

steps.title: Isn't that obvious?
steps.stepSummary: If this is רבי יוסי, it is obvious the animal is holy but not offered. So why teach it?
steps.simpleTranslation: It is obvious that it is holy and not offered!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא objects that, under רבי יוסי, the ruling seems too obvious to need saying.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי counts both halves of the statement. So the animal is half עולה and half שלמים, and it cannot be offered as either one. Since that follows plainly, the ברייתא seems to be teaching nothing new.

keyTerms.meaning: It is obvious (why say it?)
Holy, but not offered on the מזבח

phrases.english: It is obvious that it is holy and not offered!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the identification with רבי יוסי to challenge why the ruling was needed.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling in the ברייתא that the animal is holy but not offered.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Under רבי יוסי, this follows automatically, so stating it seems unnecessary.

steps.title: The new point is about the תמורה
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא was needed to teach that the תמורה is also not offered.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was needed for its תמורה. You might have said: true, the animal itself is not offered, but its תמורה should be offered. So the ברייתא teaches us that it is not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא's real new teaching is about the תמורה (the swapped animal), not the original animal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תמורה is a different animal that was never itself pushed off from the מזבח. So we might think it could be offered, even though the original could not. The ברייתא's words 'its תמורה is like it' rule that out.

keyTerms.meaning: An animal swapped for a קרבן, which then becomes holy too
He needed it (to teach this)
You might have said (a mistaken first thought)
It teaches us (the new point)

phrases.english: Its substitute is what he needed to teach,
for you might have said:
granted that it itself is not offered,
its substitute should be offered,
so it teaches us otherwise.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 17.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shifts the novelty of the ruling to a different detail (the תמורה).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Only the original animal was pushed off from the מזבח, so its תמורה could be offered.
steps.terutzMaskana: The תמורה also may not be offered.

steps.title: Why the תמורה is not offered: קדושה דחויה
steps.stepSummary: The original animal has 'pushed-off' holiness. The תמורה comes from that holiness, so it is pushed off too.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why is the animal itself not offered? Because it has pushed-off holiness. Its תמורה comes from the strength of that pushed-off holiness, so it is not offered either.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the reason behind its answer. Whatever blocks the original animal also blocks its תמורה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The original animal is holy, but it is 'pushed off' from the מזבח because it is not fully one קרבן. The תמורה gets its holiness only through that animal. So it carries the same blocked status.

keyTerms.meaning: Holiness that is pushed off (blocked) from the מזבח
From the strength (source) of
What is different? (What is the reason?)

steps.whatToRemember: A תמורה takes on the status of the animal it came from. If the original has קדושה דחויה, the תמורה can't be offered either.
steps.whyThisMatters: This idea sets up רבי יוחנן's case in the next step, where an animal is also holy but blocked from the מזבח.

phrases.english: What is the reason that it itself is not offered?
Because it has pushed-off holiness,
its substitute too
comes from the strength of pushed-off holiness.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reasoning behind the answer in Step 18.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A תמורה that comes from קדושה דחויה is also pushed off and not offered.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: a partners' animal consecrated half at a time
steps.stepSummary: A partner consecrates his half, then buys and consecrates the other half. The animal is holy but not offered, it can make a תמורה, and its תמורה... (the ruling continues).
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: Take an animal owned by two partners. One consecrated his half, then bought the other half and consecrated it. It is holy but not offered. It can make a תמורה, and its תמורה...
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן brings a new case of an animal that is holy but blocked from the מזבח. His ruling continues past this point.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When only half of the animal was holy, it could not be offered. Once it was pushed off like that, it stays pushed off, even after the whole animal becomes holy. Even so, it is holy enough to make a תמורה.

keyTerms.meaning: Partners who own something together
Consecrated (made holy)
Its half
It can make a תמורה (a swap for it becomes holy)

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the animal becomes fit once both halves are holy. It was pushed off when only half was holy, and it stays that way.

phrases.english: רבי יוחנן said:
An animal belonging to two partners,
one consecrated his half,
and then bought the other half and consecrated it;
it is holy and is not offered,
and it makes a substitute,
and its substitute

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: בְּהֵמָה שֶׁל שְׁנֵי שׁוּתָּפִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a new case that is like the partly-holy animal discussed before.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An animal consecrated half at a time is holy but never offered, and it can make a תמורה.
